title: Organization, workspaces and versioning
html:
English | Português (Brasil)

Organization, workspaces and versioning

When the operator created MinhaOrganizacao in tutorial 01, Golmet asked "what do you want to initialize?" — and the journey's first choice defines the structure of everything: the Organization is the root that groups the workspaces, it keeps the principles (CONSTITUTION.md), the navigation (INDEX.md) and the product manifest (products:). It doesn't run the requirements pipeline — the pipeline lives in the workspaces.

The two versioning models

The decision that shapes every product is the versioning: field in the org's golmet.yaml. MinhaOrganizacao uses org-repo: the whole organization is one Git repository — MeuApp is a folder versioned inside it. In this model, the .gitignore belongs to the org root (created by init --org), the kit zone (.golmet/) belongs to the root — shared — and the product is born lean, without its own zone and without its own .gitignore: the org's versioning already covers it.

The other model, produtos-repo, is the FORMAT classic (DR-008): each product is its own repository, with its own versioned .golmet/ (the kit of THAT repo, inherited by the product team when cloning) and its own .gitignore. Containers created before the field existed are treated as produtos-repo (the retroactive default).

In practice: init --into reads the declared model and delivers the product the right way, reporting which one it applied — "organization versioning model: org-repo". The .golmet/ zone changes role by context (workspace versioned · engine config state · container work zone) — the detail in layers.md.

The catalog and the truth

The organizations the kit creates (or adopts) enter the global catalog (~/.golmet/organizations.json) — the wizard uses the catalog to list orgs when someone creates a product. The invariant: the org's golmet.yaml is the source of truth (structure and products:); the catalog is convenience. When the validate runs on a container, it validates the declaration: a declared product without a directory is a failure; a product directory outside products is a warning — the org and the disk must tell the same story.

The scoping rule

A practical question the structure answers: where do I write this artifact? The rule is one: in the subject's workspace. A product subject (an RN, a spec) is written in the product workspace; a transversal org subject (a meeting checkpoint, a migration history) is written in the org's work zone .golmet/ — gitignored, because it's kit work, not company content. And what fits nowhere is born in the work zone and promoted by decision — never loose at the root.
